time.desc: The top judicial body ruled that the administration's use of an emergency authorization to impose tariffs on a wide range of imports was ultra vires, triggering a chain reaction of subsequent use of another temporary authorization to continue the levy.
The administration instead authorized a limited-time temporary authorization to impose uniform tariffs on almost all imports, and publicly stated that it planned to further increase the tax rate.

The trade authorities announced the launch of new trade investigations against a number of major trading partners to provide alternative legal paths for subsequent tariff increases, and simultaneously expanded the scope of investigations into forced labor-related imports.
The executive head issued a statement on a public platform criticizing the judiciary's ruling on tariff authorization and declared that he would continue to impose taxes from other legal sources.

The executive authorities signed an order to set extremely high tariffs on imported patented brand-name drugs, while providing tax reduction and exemption paths based on local production or price arrangements and setting up a transition period.

The administrative authorities have adjusted the national security tariff rules for existing metals and their derivatives, reduced taxes or exempted some products, and simplified tax calculation methods.

The executive head issued the threat of the highest level of additional tariffs to major trading partners on the grounds of accusations related to foreign security conflicts. The other party's officials publicly denied and opposed tying security issues with tariffs.

The customs department has promoted the launch of a large-scale refund system and registration arrangements for past tariffs that have been judicially denied, indicating that tariff refunds have entered the implementation stage.

Citing the temporary tariffs implemented by Law N Law O has brought uncertainty to countries that have previously negotiated a 10% tariff agreement with Country Y (including Country E and Country B); Agency A said it will continue to implement the binding reciprocal trade agreement, but officials said that countries with previous agreements will face new global tariffs instead of the original negotiated rates. Economists pointed out that Law O requires non-discrimination implementation and makes bilateral agreements difficult to maintain.

Institution V1 After the ruling overturned most of the tariff measures of the ruling team A Leader A raised global tariffs to 15%, triggering market turmoil, Index S fell sharply on Monday; Company H2 chief market strategist Person F3 said tariff uncertainty has shrouded the market for a long time, and it is unclear how the refund dispute will end, and the rapid shift to Plan B has not eliminated much uncertainty.

Country Y Trade Representative E1 announced that it would treat 15 trading partners (including Regional Organization A, Country S1, Country E1, Country T1, Country I1, Country D1, Country C1, Country H1, Country I, Country B1, Region T, Launch a new investigation into structural overcapacity issues in Country J1, Country W, Country G and Country Q), with the goal of completing it before the expiration of tariffs on Law O
Country Y A separate Law E investigation will be launched into about 60 trading partner countries to ensure that these countries prohibit the import of goods produced with forced labor.

Leader A first publicly attacked Institution V1 on the Product C platform, calling it completely incompetent and embarrassingly and needlessly looting Country Y for not showing sufficient loyalty to him, asserting the absolute right to impose tariffs in another form and having begun doing so (the Institution V1 ruling did not recognize this absolute right)

Country Y officials held talks with Country W officials to discuss the future direction of Agreement A; Leader A was interviewed on the same day and suggested that the planned meeting with the heads of state of Country X State Leader B may be postponed

The executive order imposing 100% tariff on imported brand-name drugs stipulates that patented drugs that are not produced in Country Y and are not included in the drug pricing agreement will face full tariffs, which can be reduced to 20% if they are transferred to Country Y. Large pharmaceutical companies will receive a 120-day buffer, and small companies will receive a 180-day grace. Those who have signed a most-favored-nation pricing agreement with Institution C2 and local producers will be exempted; Country Y Such agreements have been reached with 17 pharmaceutical manufacturers (13 finalized, 4 under negotiation)

In the tariff arrangement for brand-name drugs, drugs produced by Regional Organization A, Country G, Country I and Country E1 enjoy a 15% preferential tariff due to existing trade agreements, and Country E has separate arrangements; generic drugs are exempted for at least one year, and orphan drugs, veterinary drugs and special drugs from trade agreement countries or that meet urgent public health needs are also exempted

The adjusted national security tariffs on steel, aluminum and copper stipulate that derivatives with a metal content of less than 15% are exempt from 50% tariffs, and tariffs on some metal-intensive industrial and power grid equipment are reduced from 50% to 15% (valid until 2027). Derivatives with a content exceeding 15% are subject to a unified tariff of 25%. All metal-produced products using Country Y but manufactured overseas are subject to a lower tariff of 10%. The 50% tariff on raw materials remains unchanged but is calculated based on the sales price.

Public opinion narratives emerged in Chinese social media and financial discussions about Leader A resuming a certain 50% additional tariff and re-escalating the previously suspended tariff war; GT only serves as a record of public opinion on that day, and does not identify specific applicable countries, implementation details or market statements as policy facts that have been confirmed by many parties.

Country G The Ministry of Foreign Affairs released a new version of the Diplomatic Blue Book, downgrading the Country X - Country G relationship from one of the most important bilateral relations to important neighboring countries for the first time, and including for the first time an analysis of the impact of Leader A reciprocal tariffs on Country G - Country Y economic relations; Country X Institution K2 responded by pointing the source of the deterioration in relations to Country G The Prime Minister's Taiwan-related remarks
